question: Which leader was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and carried out a salt protest in the Madras Presidency during the Civil Disobedience Movement? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Sarojini Naidu
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
C. Rajagopalachari
K. Kamaraj
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is C. Rajagopalachari

Explanation:
C. Rajagopalachari was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and led the salt protest in the Madras Presidency during the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930. He later became the first Indian Governor-General of India. He was also a member of the Swaraj Party.

question:
Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
(RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 1928 – Bardoli Satyagraha
1929 – Gandhi–Irwin Pact
1918 – Kheda Satyagraha
1917 – Champaran Satyagraha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1929 – Gandhi–Irwin Pact

Explanation:
The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was signed in 1931, not 1929. This agreement was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931. It ended the Civil Disobedience Movement and agreed to participate in the Round Table Conference. The other pairs are correct: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Vallabhbhai Patel; Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was for revenue relief; Champaran Satyagraha (1917) opposed indigo cultivation. Thus, 1929–Gandhi–Irwin Pact is incorrectly matched.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Gandhi–Irwin Pact → Signed in 1931
☛ Bardoli Satyagraha → 1928, led by Vallabhbhai Patel
☛ Kheda Satyagraha → 1918, for land revenue relief
☛ Champaran Satyagraha → 1917, against indigo cultivation
☛ Dandi March → 1930, Salt Satyagraha

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 1929 – गांधी-इरविन समझौता।

Explanation:
गांधी-इरविन समझौता वर्ष 1931 में हुआ था, न कि 1929 में। यह समझौता महात्मा गांधी और वायसराय लॉर्ड इरविन के बीच 5 मार्च 1931 को हस्ताक्षरित हुआ। इसके तहत सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन समाप्त करने और गोलमेज सम्मेलन में भाग लेने पर सहमति बनी। अन्य युग्म सही हैं: बारदोली सत्याग्रह (1928) का नेतृत्व वल्लभभाई पटेल ने किया; खेड़ा सत्याग्रह (1918) किसानों द्वारा राजस्व मुक्ति के लिए किया गया; चंपारण सत्याग्रह (1917) नील की खेती के विरोध में गांधी द्वारा किया गया। अतः 1929-गांधी-इरविन समझौता गलत सुमेलित है।

question: Which of the following incidents prompted Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Withdrawal of the Khilafat Movement
Suspension of the Rowlatt Act
Chauri-Chaura incident
Alipore bomb case
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chauri-Chaura incident

Explanation:
On February 5, 1922, in Chauri-Chaura, Uttar Pradesh, protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. Disturbed by this violence, Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement. Gandhi believed in non-violence and considered violence detrimental to the movement. This incident showed that the masses were straying from the path of non-violence, so on February 12, 1922, he decided to suspend the movement. The Congress Working Committee also supported this decision. The movement was a significant phase in India's freedom struggle.

☛ In which state is Chauri-Chaura located? → Uttar Pradesh
☛ What was the aim of the Non-Cooperation Movement? → Non-violent resistance against British rule
☛ When did the Non-Cooperation Movement start? → August 1, 1920
☛ What was Mahatma Gandhi's main principle? → Non-violence and Satyagraha
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस घटना ने महात्मा गांधी को असहयोग आंदोलन वापस लेने के लिए प्रेरित किया? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)

रॉलेट एक्ट का निलंबन

अलीपुर बम मामला
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है चौरी-चौरा घटना

Explanation:
5 फरवरी 1922 को उत्तर प्रदेश के चौरी-चौरा में प्रदर्शनकारियों ने एक पुलिस थाने में आग लगा दी, जिसमें 22 पुलिसकर्मी मारे गए। इस हिंसा से व्यथित महात्मा गांधी ने असहयोग आंदोलन को वापस ले लिया। गांधी जी अहिंसा में विश्वास रखते थे और हिंसा को आंदोलन के लिए हानिकारक मानते थे। इस घटना ने दिखाया कि जनता अहिंसक मार्ग से भटक रही है, इसलिए उन्होंने 12 फरवरी 1922 को असहयोग आंदोलन को स्थगित करने का निर्णय लिया। कांग्रेस कार्यसमिति ने भी इस निर्णय का समर्थन किया। यह आंदोलन भारतीय स्वतंत्रता संग्राम का एक महत्वपूर्ण चरण था।

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the Atmiya Sabha? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: The Atmiya Sabha was established in 1824
The Atmiya Sabha laid the foundation for the Brahmo Samaj
The Atmiya Sabha was established at Calcutta
The Atmiya Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Atmiya Sabha was established in 1824

Explanation:
The Atmiya Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1815, not 1824, at Calcutta. It was a philosophical discussion group that later laid the foundation for the Brahmo Samaj (established in 1828). Its aim was to promote social reform, monotheism, and Vedic principles. Therefore, the statement mentioning 1824 is incorrect.

☛ Place of establishment of Atmiya Sabha → Calcutta
☛ Successor of Atmiya Sabha → Brahmo Samaj (1828)
☛ Objective of Atmiya Sabha → Monotheism and social reform

question:
Which of the following best describes the Mahar Movement in Maharashtra?
(RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: A tribal uprising against British forest laws
A peasant movement against zamindari exploitation
A religious reform movement aimed at purifying Hindu rituals
A socio-political movement for Dalit rights and social equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A socio-political movement for Dalit rights and social equality

Explanation:
The Mahar Movement in Maharashtra was a significant socio-political movement led by the Dalit community, particularly the Mahar caste, under the leadership of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It aimed at securing social equality, educational opportunities, and political rights for Dalits. The movement strongly opposed caste-based discrimination and demanded rights such as temple entry, access to public spaces, and education. It emerged during the British colonial period and played a crucial role in awakening Dalit consciousness. After independence, it laid the foundation for constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Castes. The Mahar Movement was not a tribal uprising against forest laws, a peasant movement against zamindari, or a religious reform movement; it was specifically focused on Dalit empowerment and social justice.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who led the Mahar Movement? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ What was the main objective of the Mahar Movement? → Social equality and rights for Dalits
☛ In which state did the Mahar Movement take place? → Maharashtra
☛ Which caste was the Mahar community part of? → Untouchable (Scheduled Caste)
☛ Which later movement was inspired by the Mahar Movement? → Dalit Panther Movement

Explanation:
महार आंदोलन महाराष्ट्र में दलित समुदाय, विशेषकर महार जाति द्वारा चलाया गया एक महत्वपूर्ण सामाजिक-राजनीतिक आंदोलन था। इसका उद्देश्य दलितों को सामाजिक समानता, शैक्षिक अवसर और राजनीतिक अधिकार दिलाना था। यह आंदोलन डॉ. बी.आर. आंबेडकर के नेतृत्व में शुरू हुआ, जो स्वयं महार समुदाय से थे। आंदोलन ने जातिगत भेदभाव के खिलाफ आवाज उठाई और दलितों के लिए मंदिर प्रवेश, सार्वजनिक स्थानों पर उपयोग और शिक्षा जैसे अधिकारों की मांग की। महार आंदोलन ने ब्रिटिश काल में दलित चेतना को जागृत किया और स्वतंत्रता के बाद संवैधानिक सुरक्षा उपायों की नींव रखी। यह आंदोलन किसी आदिवासी विद्रोह, किसान आंदोलन या धार्मिक सुधार आंदोलन नहीं था, बल्कि विशिष्ट रूप से दलित अधिकारों पर केंद्रित था।

question: Which of the following methods was characteristically adopted by the Moderates during the early phase of the Indian national movement? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Boycott of foreign goods and institutions
Swadeshi Movement
Promotion of Vedic education
Constitutional reforms
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constitutional reforms

Explanation:
During the early phase of the Indian national movement (1885-1905), the Moderates characteristically adopted the method of constitutional reforms. They remained loyal to the British Crown and sought changes through petitions, prayers, and delegations. Their approach was to educate public opinion and present demands before the British government. Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozeshah Mehta, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale advocated for reforms in Indian Councils Acts, civil services, and economic policies. They aimed for gradual self-government within the British Empire. The Moderates were criticized by later extremists for their soft approach, but they laid the groundwork for political awakening. The Swadeshi and Boycott movements were later adopted by the Extremists after 1905.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Key Moderate leader → Dadabhai Naoroji
☛ Main method of Moderates → Petition and prayer
☛ Goal of Moderates → Gradual constitutional reforms
☛ Limitation of Moderates → Not lack of patriotism, but strategy
☛ Boycott movement started by → Extremists in 1905
question_hi: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के प्रारंभिक चरण के दौरान नरमपंथियों द्वारा निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी पद्धति को विशेष रूप से अपनाया गया था? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)

संवैधानिक सुधार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संवैधानिक सुधार

Explanation:
भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के प्रारंभिक चरण (1885-1905) में नरमपंथियों ने मुख्यतः संवैधानिक सुधारों की पद्धति अपनाई। वे ब्रिटिश शासन के प्रति वफादार थे और याचिकाओं, प्रार्थनाओं और प्रतिनिधिमंडलों के माध्यम से सरकार से सुधारों की मांग करते थे। उनका मानना था कि अंग्रेज भारतीयों की समस्याओं को सुनेंगे और क्रमिक सुधार लाएंगे। दादाभाई नौरोजी, फिरोजशाह मेहता और गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले जैसे नरमपंथी नेता भारतीय परिषद अधिनियमों में संशोधन और सिविल सेवाओं में भारतीयों की भागीदारी के लिए प्रयासरत रहे। उन्होंने प्रेस और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता जैसे मुद्दों को उठाया। स्वदेशी और बहिष्कार आंदोलन बाद में गरमपंथियों द्वारा अपनाए गए।

question: Majnu Shah is associated with which of the following rebellions? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:
Majnu Shah was a prominent fakir who led the Fakir–Sannyasi Rebellion against the British in the 18th century. This rebellion spread across the regions of Bengal and Bihar between 1763 and 1800. It involved fakirs and sannyasis who united to oppose the exploitative tax policies and oppression of the British East India Company. Majnu Shah is considered a key leader of this movement. The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) was led by the Santhal tribe, the Indigo Revolt (1859-60) involved indigo farmers, and the Kol Rebellion (1831-32) was associated with the Kol tribe. question: Which of the following samitis was founded by Ashwini Kumar Dutt in Barisal? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 3)

Jugantar Samiti
Bharat Mata Samiti
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swadesh Bandhab Samiti

Explanation:
Ashwini Kumar Dutt was a prominent Bengali revolutionary and nationalist leader. In 1905, he founded the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti in Barisal (now in Bangladesh) to oppose the partition of Bengal. The samiti aimed to promote the Swadeshi movement, boycott foreign goods, and spread national awakening. Dutt focused on education, self-employment, and rural development. He was a popular leader and was known as the 'Lion of Barisal'. The Anushilan Samiti was founded by Pramathanath Mitra in Kolkata, while the Jugantar Samiti was formed by Barindra Ghosh and other revolutionaries. The 'Bharat Mata Samiti' is not associated with Ashwini Kumar Dutt.

question: Which of the following best explains the Indian National Congress’s stance on communal politics during the Moderate phase? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Accepted political demands based on religious identities
Maintained a secular approach in its programmes and demands
Aligned itself with leaders of specific religious communities
Limited organisational participation to a single religious group
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maintained a secular approach in its programmes and demands

Explanation:
During the Moderate phase (1885-1905), the Indian National Congress adopted a secular stance and did not support demands based on religious identities. Leaders like Dadabhai Naoroji, Firozeshah Mehta, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale believed in uniting people of all religions. They focused on issues such as administrative reforms, economic exploitation, and civil rights, rather than communal matters. The Congress promoted Hindu-Muslim unity and opposed communal representation. Thus, the Congress maintained a secular approach in its programmes and demands during the Moderate phase, seeking equal rights for all religious communities.

question: Who among the following muslim leaders first propounded the theory of 'Two nations'? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Liaqat Ali

Rahmat Ali Chaudhary
solution:

Explanation:
The theory of 'Two Nations' was first propounded by Mohammad Iqbal in his 1930 Allahabad address. He argued that Hindus and Muslims in India are two distinct nations with separate cultures, religions, and traditions. This theory later became the ideological basis for the creation of Pakistan. Rahmat Ali Chaudhary coined the term 'Pakistan' in 1933, while Muhammad Ali Jinnah politically implemented the two-nation theory. Liaqat Ali was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan but did not propound the two-nation theory.

question: In which year did the Non-Cooperation Movement begin in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1930
1920
1940
1910
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1920

Explanation:
The Non-Cooperation Movement in India began in 1920 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. It was the first major mass movement of nonviolent resistance against British rule. The movement was launched in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Rowlatt Act. Gandhi announced the movement on August 1, 1920. People boycotted government jobs, schools, courts, and foreign goods. The movement was called off after the Chauri Chaura incident (1922). This movement was a significant milestone in India's freedom struggle.

question: Which provision in Part II of the Constitution defines one basis for citizenship at the commencement, specifically that the person’s either parent was born in India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Article 8
Article 9
Article 6
Article 5
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 5

Explanation:
Part II of the Indian Constitution contains Articles 5 to 11, which deal with citizenship. Article 5 defines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution (January 26, 1950). It states that a person born in India, whose either parent was born in India, or who has been ordinarily resident in India for at least five years immediately before the commencement, is a citizen. This provision establishes the basis for citizenship when the Constitution came into effect. Article 6 provides citizenship to migrants from Pakistan, Article 8 covers persons of Indian origin residing outside India, and Article 9 deals with loss of citizenship upon voluntarily acquiring foreign citizenship.

☛ Which article grants citizenship to migrants from Pakistan? → Article 6

question: Which constitutional article empowers the Indian Parliament to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (19/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 6
Article 11
Article 8
Article 5
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 11

Explanation:
Article 11 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of citizenship. While Articles 5 to 10 define citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution on 26 January 1950, Article 11 gives Parliament the authority to modify these provisions and enact new laws. Under this article, the Citizenship Act, 1955 was passed, which details the modes of acquiring citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and territorial annexation, as well as termination of citizenship. This article ensures that the Parliament has comprehensive power to regulate citizenship matters as needed.

question: If an Emergency Proclamation is approved only by the Rajya Sabha while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, for how long does the Proclamation remain in force from the first sitting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: 60 days
14 days
30 days
21 days
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 30 days

Explanation:
According to Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, when the Lok Sabha is dissolved and an Emergency Proclamation is approved only by the Rajya Sabha, the Proclamation remains in force for 30 days from the first sitting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha. Within this period, the new Lok Sabha must approve the Proclamation; otherwise, it ceases to be effective. This provision ensures democratic oversight.

question: What is the maximum total duration for which President’s Rule can continue in a State under Article 356, subject to parliamentary approvals and constitutional conditions? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Up to two years
Up to one year
Up to three years
Up to four years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Up to three years

Explanation:
Under Article 356, President's Rule can initially be imposed for two months, extendable up to six months with parliamentary approval. Thereafter, it can be extended every six months, subject to parliamentary approval, for a maximum total duration of three years. This three-year limit was introduced by the 44th Amendment (1978). Any extension beyond three years requires a constitutional amendment. The provision ensures that the federal structure is not undermined by prolonged central intervention. The maximum continuous period of President's Rule in a state is thus three years.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Maximum without parliamentary approval → 60 days
☛ Maximum total duration → 3 years
☛ Amendment that imposed the limit → 44th Amendment (1978)
☛ Who recommends revocation of President's Rule → Governor

question: Before each general election to the House of the People or to a State Legislative Assembly, the President may appoint Regional Commissioners after: (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 3)

consultation with the Chief Justice of India
consultation with the Election Commission
consultation with the Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is consultation with the Election Commission

Explanation:
According to Article 324(4) of the Indian Constitution, the President may appoint Regional Commissioners before each general election to the House of the People or a State Legislative Assembly after consultation with the Election Commission. These Regional Commissioners assist the Election Commission in the smooth conduct of elections. The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body responsible for administering election processes at both national and state levels. This provision ensures that the appointment is made based on the advice of the Election Commission, which has the expertise and authority over electoral matters. The consultation does not involve the Speaker of Lok Sabha, Chief Justice of India, or the Prime Minister.

question: The appointing authority for the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission under Article 316 of the Constitution of India is: (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: The Chief Minister of the State
The President of India
The Governor of the State
The Speaker of the State Assembly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Governor of the State

Explanation:
Under Article 316 of the Constitution of India, the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor of the state. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and makes these appointments in consultation with the central government. This provision ensures the independence of the commission. After appointment, members serve a term of 6 years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier. The Governor also has the authority to remove them, but only as per constitutional procedures. This process helps maintain the impartiality and autonomy of the Public Service Commission.

वित्त आयोग (प्रकीर्ण उपबंध) अधिनियम, 1951 के अनुसार, वित्त आयोग में एक अध्यक्ष और चार अन्य सदस्य शामिल होते हैं। इस प्रकार आयोग में कुल पांच सदस्य होते हैं। अध्यक्ष को सार्वजनिक मामलों का अनुभव होना चाहिए, जबकि अन्य चार सदस्यों को न्यायपालिका, वित्त, लेखा या प्रशासन में विशेषज्ञता होनी चाहिए। यह आयोग भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा गठित किया जाता है और हर पांच वर्ष में इसकी सिफारिशें आती हैं। आयोग का मुख्य कार्य केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच कर राजस्व के वितरण की सिफारिश करना है।

question: Under Article 275 of the Constitution, the sums provided by the Parliament as grants-in-aid to states are required to be charged on which fund? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Public Account of India
Contingency Fund of India
Consolidated Fund of India
State Emergency Fund
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Consolidated Fund of India

Explanation:
Under Article 275, the sums provided by Parliament as grants-in-aid to states are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. This expenditure is not subject to the annual vote of Parliament, making it a charged expenditure. The Consolidated Fund of India records all receipts and expenditures, while the Public Account holds deposits and the Contingency Fund is for emergencies. These grants are given to states for their schemes and development works. Article 275 enables the central government to provide financial assistance to states, especially those in need. The amount and terms are determined by Parliament through law. This ensures states have resources for public welfare and infrastructure without annual uncertainty.

question: After a Constitution Amendment Bill relating to the Directive Principles of State Policy is passed by the Parliament, what is the next mandatory constitutional step for it to become a law? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Notification in the Gazette
Ratification by State Legislatures
President’s Assent
Approval by the Supreme Court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President’s Assent

Explanation:
According to Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, after a Constitution Amendment Bill is passed by Parliament, the next mandatory step is obtaining the President's Assent. Unlike amendments that affect the federal structure, amendments related to the Directive Principles of State Policy do not require ratification by state legislatures. The President must give assent to the bill, after which it becomes an Act and is then notified in the Gazette. Approval by the Supreme Court is not a routine step; it is only sought in cases involving the basic structure doctrine. Thus, the President's Assent is the crucial next step for the bill to become law.

☛ Can the President withhold assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill? → No, he must give assent
question_hi: संसद द्वारा राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांतों से संबंधित संविधान संशोधन विधेयक पारित करने के बाद, इसके कानून बनने के लिए अगला अनिवार्य संवैधानिक चरण क्या है? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 1)
options_hi: राजपत्र में अधिसूचना
राज्य विधानमंडलों द्वारा अनुसमर्थन
राष्ट्रपति की सहमति
सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा अनुमोदन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राष्ट्रपति की सहमति

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 368 के अनुसार, संविधान संशोधन विधेयक संसद द्वारा पारित होने के बाद अनिवार्य रूप से राष्ट्रपति की सहमति प्राप्त करना चाहिए। राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांतों से संबंधित संशोधन विधेयकों को राज्य विधानमंडलों द्वारा अनुसमर्थन की आवश्यकता नहीं होती, क्योंकि वे संविधान के संघीय ढांचे को प्रभावित नहीं करते। राष्ट्रपति की सहमति के बाद ही विधेयक अधिनियम बनता है और फिर राजपत्र में अधिसूचित किया जाता है। सुप्रीम कोर्ट की अनुमोदन की आवश्यकता केवल संविधान की मूल संरचना के उल्लंघन के मामलों में होती है, न कि सामान्य प्रक्रिया में। इस प्रकार, संसद द्वारा पारित होने के बाद राष्ट्रपति की सहमति अगला अनिवार्य चरण है।
